subject: business-studies
title: From Idea to Shelf Adventure
welcome_lead: How does a product get from factory to shop? 🛒
meta_desc: Goods & Services Adventure 2 — KS3 Business Studies on the supply chain from producer to consumer.
final_note: You learned the supply chain — producer, wholesaler, retailer, consumer.

concepts.def: All steps from making to selling
Buys in bulk and sells to shops

walkthroughs.body_html:
A product travels through a supply chain:

1) Producer makes it → 2) Wholesaler stores it → 3) Retailer sells it → 4) Consumer uses it. 🚚

Wholesalers buy thousands of items cheaply and break them into smaller boxes for shops.

Retailers sell to you — Tesco, Boots, Amazon, the corner shop.

Each step adds a bit of price.

Some businesses skip steps to save money:

  • Apple sells direct online.
  • Tesla sells direct, no dealers.
  • Many farmers sell at markets.

Shorter chain = cheaper for buyer, more profit for seller. ✂️

options: The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.

mcqs.q: What do McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y describe?
options: Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Two contrasting management assumptions: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control; Theory Y assumes workers can be self-motivated and seek responsibility.
Theory X is about working in a factory and Theory Y is about office work.
